name: The Fatal Thespian | Ch2 Starters Revisited
description_md:
The Fatal Thespian

>In this mini-series I'm focusing on powerful decks built from the Chapter 2 starters. Here André can deal up to 9 damage in a turn by [bashing enemies' legs in](/card/60363), [pushing them off roofs](/card/60378) (twice) and [shooting them](/card/12045). Who knew show business was so cutthroat?! `If you want to support my work, give it a like ❤︎ and a favorite ★ on here!`

Series Decks

|   Seeker   |   Survivor   |   Guardian   |    Rogue   |   Mystic   | |:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Carolyn | Miguel | Tommy| André | Marie |

At a Glance

>| Stats | | >|:---|:---| >| Clue-finding: |  ★★★★☆ | >| Consistency: |  ★★★★☆ | >| Enemy Management: |  ★★★★★ | >| Encounter Defense: |  ★★★☆☆ | >| Survivability: |  ★★☆☆☆ | >| Simplicity: |  ★★★★★ |

Overview

- Taking slapstick literally: With his [Polished Cane](/card/60363), André slaps people with a stick at an 8 with [Olivier](/card/12046). This will often trigger an oversuccess, giving you both an extra action and automatically evading the enemy. Both [Hammerless](/card/12045) and [A Sudden Fall](/card/60378) then deal extra damage to exhausted foes. [The Grapevine](/card/60374) allows you to get straight to bad guys (even Aloof ones) and engage them while providing card draw. Of course you can also evade enemies with your great stat too. - Cash for clues: When you're not blugeoning enemies with walking implements, you're getting cash and finding clues. [Out the Door](/card/60373) and ["Watch this!"](/card/60371) throw resources at you, while [Thieves' Kit](/card/12049) provides money from investigating. [Prestidigitation](/card/12052) allows you to flip between clue-finding and enemy management with ease. When you're not investigating with a Kit (e.g. you have your weapons out), resources convert to clues with [Right Under Their Noses](/card/60368), [Pay Your Dues](/card/60365) and [Silver Tongue](/card/60380). André's extra action coupled to [Olivier's](/card/12046) free move gives great versatility, often enabling up to 4 clues in a turn. - There's no people like show people: As André has a slightly padded deck with 3 signature skills, card draw is important. [Lucky Cigarette Case](/card/12044) gives cards for oversuccess, while upgraded [Grapevine](/card/60374) pairs card draw with efficient enemy management. [Manual Dexterity](/card/12091) and a [Perception](/card/12093) round this off, replacing themselves while boosting tests. In terms of the encounter deck, André sports a respectable number of and icons here in addition to [Know the Line](/card/60353). While the Film Star only has [Olivier Bishop](/card/12046) as soak, his basic health and sanity are good. Thank you: [5argon](https://arkhamdb.com/user/profile/61394/5argon) and [their thumbnail tool](https://arkham-starter.com/tool/thumbnails); [Valentin1331](https://arkhamdb.com/user/profile/42890/Valentin1331) for his support over the years; the community creators of [Arkham.Build](https://www.patreon.com/c/arkhambuild/) ([Felix](https://spoettel.dev/)), [Arkham Cards](https://www.patreon.com/c/arkhamcards/) ([zzorba](https://www.reddit.com/user/zzorba/)) and [ArkhamDB](https://www.patreon.com/c/kamalisk/) ([kamalisk](https://www.reddit.com/user/kamalisk/)) - linking their Patreons!

Starting deck and planned progression

0 XP starting deck is below (and link here): A recommended order of purchases/upgrades is: - [Out the Door](/card/60370) → [Out the Door •](/card/60373) - 1 x [Silver Tongue](/card/12047) → 1 x [Silver Tongue •••](/card/60380) - 1 x [Silver Tongue](/card/12047) → 1 x [The Grapevine ••](/card/60374) - 1 x [Perception](/card/12093) → 1 x [The Grapevine ••](/card/60374) - [Quick Exit](/card/60366) → [A Sudden Fall ••](/card/60378) - 2 x [Another Day, Another Dollar](/card/12056) Post-19 XP suggestions are: - [Right Under Their Noses](/card/60368) → [Right Under Their Noses •••](/card/60382) - 1 x [Unexpected Courage](/card/12094) → 1 x [Contingency](/card/60383)

Playtesting notes

I made a couple of small tweaks on play testing. Firstly I swapped the order of [Another Day, Another Dollar](/card/12056) and [upgraded Right Under Their Noses](/card/60382) (so the former is bought inside your first 19 XP). This plays a little better with [upgraded Silver Tongue](/card/60380), which itself works very well with [Thieves' Kit](/card/12049). Surprisingly, André felt like my main clue-finder while playing - in addition to his great enemy management. The other small change was removing one copy of [Perception](/card/12093) rather than [Unexpected Courage](/card/12094) from the final deck. Given you do tests with [Polished Cane](/card/60363), the icons are handy over the slightly more situational icons. Playing on Hard two-player through Children of Blood, I thought the deck worked great. I used the 5 bonus XP from Hard difficulty for [upgraded Silver Tongue](/card/60380) and a copy of [upgraded The Grapevine](/card/60374). While the latter didn't shine too much in the campaign, drawing a card for something you were going to do anyway is a nice effect. I found [Polished Cane](/card/60363) in particular to be excellent - very easily triggering your extra action by testing at an 8 with [Olivier](/card/12046). As mentioned in my review of Polished Cane, it also allows you to pin Elusive enemies to a location if you get the over-success on your first action. [Prestidigitation](/card/12052) was extremely useful in shuffling hand assets around on the fly. Overall this build felt like the quintessential Rogue, which is exactly what I was going for!

Final thoughts

This deck allows you to have your cake and eat it. Enemy management (both fighting and evading) leverage André's high and his easy money feeds into clue-finding. People often enjoy [Trish](/card/12007) because her Seeker splash gives clues, however André's additional action does this and more. [The Grapevine](/card/60374) is an added bonus, giving you card draw with absurd mobility, and convenient means to engage Aloof enemies like [Whippoorwills](/card/12166), [Zealots](/card/12188) and most Civilians. Hope you enjoy!
